name: Spot reduction exercises

lead: Spot reduction is the idea that exercising one area, like the abs or the face, burns fat in that area for a slimmer belly, cheeks or jawline. It is promoted in fitness media and looksmaxxing spaces as ab routines and face or jaw exercises.

Proponents think working a muscle draws on nearby fat. Researchers cited by reference works say fat is mobilised from the whole body according to overall energy balance, genetics and hormones; a 2022 meta-analysis of 13 studies found no significant localized fat reduction, and a small 2023 trial suggested a possible exception. Building muscle in an area can change how it looks.

paras: Users do crunch and ab circuits, or facial and jaw exercises, usually alongside a diet aimed at overall fat loss.
Little direct harm is documented. The cited concern is misleading marketing, including ab-belt claims the FTC has challenged and EMS devices not FDA-cleared for fat loss.

angle.text: Users train one area, such as the abs or jaw, hoping to burn fat there for a slimmer belly, cheeks or jawline. Studies cited by reference works find fat is lost across the body, though building muscle in an area can change its look.

lead: Spot reduction exercises are routines aimed at slimming one particular area, such as crunches for the stomach, thigh work for the legs, glute work for the hips, or facial and jaw exercises for the cheeks, in the hope that training an area leans out the fat stored there.[1][2] People use them to get a flatter midsection, trimmer thighs, a more defined jawline or a slimmer face.

The idea sits next to spot toning, which means building muscle in an area to change firmness and definition rather than to change the fat over it; muscle gained under a lean area can improve how it looks even when fat is lost across the whole body.[2] Where fat comes off first is described as strongly influenced by genetics, sex and hormones, with the lower abdomen, lower back and flanks often cited as slow to lean out.[1][2]

Wikipedia reports that physiologists and fitness professionals generally hold that fat loss occurs across the body with diet and exercise, and Grokipedia summarizes a 2022 meta-analysis that found no significant localized fat reduction, along with a small 2023 trial that suggested a possible exception.[1][2] Smaller studies continue to examine regional exercise, and some results are reported as complementary to general exercise.[3][4]

paras: Spot reduction contrasts with spot toning, which builds muscle in an area to change its firmness and definition rather than to remove overlying fat.[2] Where fat is stored and lost first is described as strongly influenced by genetics, sex and hormones.[1][2]

Grokipedia traces area-specific reducing exercises to early physical culture figures such as Eugen Sandow and to Bernarr Macfadden's magazines in the 1920s and 1930s, followed by post-war vibrating belts and reducing garments, then 1980s and 1990s workout videos, the ThighMaster and infomercial ab devices.[2] Social media, HIIT content and electrical muscle stimulation devices are cited as modern carriers of the idea.[2]

Grokipedia states that facial fat does not respond to targeted exercise and that facial exercises build muscle without reducing fat; it adds that lower water retention can make the face look slimmer in the short term.[2] Proponents of face and jaw exercises say that toning facial muscles changes contour.

On T Nation, one member logged a four-week experiment in spot reduction for the glutes using skinfold tracking, and another mentioned a study that suggested spot reduction might be possible while noting people jump on single studies.[5][6] A member also wrote about focusing on back extensions because his lower back was not as lean as he wanted.[7]

Studies described by Wikipedia and Grokipedia include a comparison of tennis players' arms, in which the dominant forearm was larger from muscle but skinfold measurements showed no difference in fat between arms.[1][2] In a 2011 randomized trial in the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 24 sedentary adults did abdominal exercises five days a week for six weeks; abdominal subcutaneous fat did not decrease, though core endurance improved.[1]

A 2007 study of 104 adults did 12 weeks of supervised resistance training on the nondominant arm; skinfolds showed fat loss in the trained arm only in men, while MRI showed generalized subcutaneous fat loss with no difference between arms.[3] A 2025 randomized trial in 60 obese women compared general aerobic, regional aerobic and combined training for 12 weeks; general training produced more systemic fat loss, the combined group improved most, and the authors described regional work as complementary.[4]

Grokipedia lists further work: a 1984 sit-up study, and a 2022 meta-analysis of 13 studies (1,158 participants) finding no significant localized fat reduction, and describes a 2023 trial in 16 overweight men in which adding abdominal endurance work to running gave greater trunk fat loss, noting it was small and unreplicated.[2]
Grokipedia states that the US FDA has not cleared electrical muscle stimulation devices for spot fat loss and that the Federal Trade Commission has challenged misleading ab-belt claims.[2]

lore.intro: Spot reduction is a recurring topic in lifting forums, usually as a question of whether area-specific work changes local leanness.[5][6][8]

claims.claim: Training an area burns the fat sitting over it.
Facial exercises slim the face or jaw.
